metadata.journal: Advances in Colloid and Interface Science

claim.summary: PFAS comprise more than 15,000 chemicals with widespread industrial applications

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) comprise more than 15,000 chemicals (U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, EPA)

claim.summary: PFAS possess strong carbon-fluorine bonds conferring exceptional chemical stability and resistance to natural degradation

evidence.verbatim_snippet: PFAS possess strong carbon‑fluorine bonds that confer exceptional chemical stability and resistance to natural degradation

claim.summary: PFAS applied in chemical coatings, metal processing, non-stick cookware, waterproof packaging, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, and personal care products

evidence.verbatim_snippet: applications of PFAS in modern industrial sectors including chemical coatings, metal processing, non-stick cookware, and waterproof packaging

claim.summary: PFAS concentrations ranging between 0.1 and 5200 ng/L measured across various water sources

evidence.verbatim_snippet: PFAS concentrations ranging between 0.1 and 5200 ng/L across various water sources (such as rivers, groundwater, snow, tap water, and coastal seawater)

claim.summary: Long-chain PFAS including PFOA and PFOS are notable examples of environmental contaminants

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Notable examples of long-chain PFAS include perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA)

claim.summary: Certain PFAS pose serious risks to living organisms, especially mammals, due to widespread occurrence and adverse health effects

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Certain PFAS thus pose serious risks to living organisms, especially mammals

claim.summary: Long-chain PFAS more technically effective than short-chain alternatives but phased out due to toxicity

evidence.verbatim_snippet: short-chain PFAS are technically less effective than their long-chain counterparts, leading to higher consumption

claim.summary: Short-chain PFAS exhibit greater mobility in water compared to long-chain PFAS, making removal more challenging

evidence.verbatim_snippet: they exhibit greater mobility compared to long-chain PFAS. Importantly, research on the occurrence, detection, and removal of short-chain PFAS is significantly less extensive

claim.summary: Short-chain PFAS may pose comparable toxicity and health risks to long-chain PFAS

evidence.verbatim_snippet: research suggests that the short-chain alternatives may pose comparable toxicity and health risks to those associated with long-chain PFAS

claim.summary: PFAS labeled as 'forever chemicals' due to remarkable chemical stability with C-F bond dissociation energy exceeding 530 kJ/mol

evidence.verbatim_snippet: PFAS are often labeled as 'forever chemicals' due to their remarkable chemical stability, which is attributed to the strength of the carbon‑fluorine (C–F) bond... with a dissociation energy exceeding 530 kJ/mol

claim.summary: PFAS can have anionic, cationic, or zwitterionic functional groups, complicating their removal processes

evidence.verbatim_snippet: PFAS can have anionic (with polar carboxylate and sulfonate head groups), cationic, or zwitterionic functional groups, complicating their removal processes

claim.summary: Advanced oxidation processes may inadvertently produce short-chain PFAS from long-chain precursors

evidence.verbatim_snippet: techniques (such as AOPs) may inadvertently produce short-chain PFAS (from their long-chain precursors), creating additional complications

claim.summary: Membrane filtration achieves PFAS removal efficiencies greater than 99% for long-chain PFAS

evidence.verbatim_snippet: achieving removal efficiencies greater than 99 % for long-chain-PFAS (including anionic, cationic, and zwitterionic PFAS molecules)

extractions.compound: Petroleum-based polymers (PSf, PES, PVDF, PVC, PMMA, PANI, PTFE)

claim.summary: Conventional membrane processes rely on petroleum-based polymers and non-biodegradable materials leading to sustainability concerns

evidence.verbatim_snippet: many conventional membrane processes rely on petroleum-based polymers and non-biodegradable materials which lead to significant sustainability concerns

claim.summary: Approximately 1.5 million kg of used petroleum-based membranes disposed of annually in the environment

evidence.verbatim_snippet: approximately 1.5 million kg of used membranes being disposed of in the environment annually

claim.summary: PFOS included in Stockholm Convention in 2009 restricting its production and use globally

evidence.verbatim_snippet: PFOS was included in the Stockholm Convention in 2009, followed by PFOA and PFHxS in 2019 and 2022, respectively

claim.summary: PFOA and PFHxS included in Stockholm Convention in 2019 and 2022 respectively

evidence.verbatim_snippet: followed by PFOA and PFHxS in 2019 and 2022, respectively

claim.summary: Commonwealth countries implemented comprehensive ban on manufacture, use, and import of PFHxS, PFOA, and PFOS starting July 1, 2025

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Commonwealth countries implemented a comprehensive ban on the manufacture, use, and import of PFHxS, PFOA, and PFOS started July 1, 2025

claim.summary: PFOA water solubility is 0.023 mol/L indicating moderate aqueous persistence

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA): solubility in water 0.023 mol/L

claim.summary: PFOS water solubility is 0.0014 mol/L indicating very low aqueous solubility

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS): solubility in water 0.0014 mol/L

extractions.compound: Long-chain PFAS (PFOA, PFOS, PFNA, PFDA, PFUnA)

claim.summary: Long-chain PFAS present higher environmental and health hazards compared to short-chain alternatives

evidence.verbatim_snippet: long-chain PFAS presenting higher environmental and health hazards

claim.summary: Chitosan-PEI aerogel achieved >95% removal efficiency for 12 different PFAS types

evidence.verbatim_snippet: The modified aerogel exhibited high efficiency in removing both short- and long-chain PFAS from water achieving a remarkable PFOA removal capacity of 5.9 g per gram of aerogel... removal efficiency for all PFAS studied exceeded 95%

claim.summary: CNC-PTMAEMA composite achieved PFOA removal capacity of 303 mg/g, substantially higher than GAC at 53 mg/g

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Langmuir model was not the optimal fit, it did predict a maximum sorption capacity of 303 mg PFOA/g, which is substantially higher than findings from a comparable study utilizing GAC as an adsorbent (53 mg PFOA/g)

claim.summary: NF270 commercial membrane achieved 99.6% rejection of PFHxA at 9.6 ± 0.2 L/m²/h/bar permeation rate

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Nanofiltration: NF270, rejection rate 99.6%, permeation 9.6 ± 0.2 L m⁻² h⁻¹ bar⁻¹

claim.summary: RO membranes achieved >98-99% rejection of long-chain PFAS including PFOA, PFOS, and PFHxA

metadata.title: Utilization of plasma in water desalination and purification

claim.summary: PFAS detected as emerging pollutants in groundwater requiring treatment

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Atmospheric pressure Ar plasma was used to treat emerging pollutants such as perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS)

claim.summary: PFOA concentration reduced to near-zero levels using plasma treatment

evidence.verbatim_snippet: concentration of PFAS, PFOA and PFOS was reduced to near 0 nmol/L as could be detected via mass spectrometry

claim.summary: PFOS reduced to near-zero concentrations via plasma treatment

evidence.verbatim_snippet: concentration of PFAS, PFOA and PFOS was reduced to near 0 nmol/L

claim.summary: Removal efficiency for long chain PFS higher than short chain PFS

evidence.verbatim_snippet: removal efficiency for long chain PFSs were observed to be higher than for shorter chain PFSs

claim.summary: Perfluoroalkyl sulfonates removed at higher rate than perfluorocarboxylic acids

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Perfluoroalkyl sulfonates were removed from the water, in general, at a higher rate than perfluorocarboxylic acid

claim.summary: Perfluorocarboxylic acids removed at lower rate than perfluoroalkyl sulfonates

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Perfluorocarboxylic acid which the authors credit to a higher surface activity by perfluoroalkyl sulfonate

claim.summary: 9 of 13 groundwater samples reached US health advisory concentration levels within 1 min plasma treatment

evidence.verbatim_snippet: 9 of those samples exhibited a reduction in concentration of PFSs to within US health advisory concentration levels (USHAL) within 1 min

claim.summary: Final 4 samples required up to 60 min plasma treatment to reach US health advisory levels

evidence.verbatim_snippet: The final 4 samples took up to 60 min of plasma treatment to reach the USHAL concentration

claim.summary: Plasma polymerization of fluorocarbon compounds exhibits low surface free energy and high thermal stability

evidence.verbatim_snippet: plasma polymerization of fluorocarbon compounds exhibits advantageous features such as the low surface free energy, high thermal stability

claim.summary: Fluorocarbon compounds exhibit high chemical resistance and low friction coefficient

evidence.verbatim_snippet: high chemical resistance, and the low friction coefficient

claim.summary: CF4 plasma treatment can convert hydrophilic membranes to hydrophobic surfaces

evidence.verbatim_snippet: conversion of a hydrophilic (WCA - 60°/0°, top/bottom) flat polyethersulfone (PES) membrane to a hydrophobic membrane surface was reported via CF4 plasma treatment

claim.summary: F8 plasma polymerization creates hydrophobic coating on PAN membrane for vacuum membrane distillation

evidence.verbatim_snippet: The plasma polymerized PAN membrane exhibited a high-water vapour flux of 32.9 kg m−2 h−1 with 99.93% salt rejection

claim.summary: PFOTES/APTES mixture generates hydrophobic coating on polyethersulfone membrane for MD

evidence.verbatim_snippet: This PES membrane exhibited a hydrophobic coating with a WCA of 110 °C after the optimum plasma treatment time of 54 s. The resultant plasma polymerized membrane exhibited a high water vapour flux of 20 kg m−2 h−1

claim.summary: CF4 plasma modified PES membrane achieves 40.9 kg/m²/h water flux with 99.97% salt rejection

evidence.verbatim_snippet: The plasma modified PES membrane showed a high-water vapour flux of 40.9 kg m−2 h−1 with an excellent salt rejection of 99.97%

claim.summary: CF4 plasma treatment reduces mechanical strength of PES membrane due to CF3 radical damage

evidence.verbatim_snippet: a reduction in the mechanical strength of the PES membrane was observed after the CF4 plasma modification, which could be attributed to the interaction of CF3 radical species from the plasma with a polymer chains

claim.summary: PTFE membranes modified with Ar plasma for DCMD process show structure-property relationships

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Plasma modification of a MD membrane with varying plasma parameters and the impact on membrane characteristics were investigated by using commercial poly(tetra-fluoro-ethylene) (PTFE) membranes

claim.summary: Fluorine from PTFE reacts with radical species from plasma after 1-2 min of treatment

evidence.verbatim_snippet: fluorine from the PTFE reacts with a radical species from the plasma after 1–2 min of treatment which altered the chemical properties

claim.summary: H2/N2 plasma treatment optimized at 7 min and 100W improves PTFE layer performance

evidence.verbatim_snippet: 7 min of the plasma treatment time and 100 W of plasma power were found as the optimum process conditions

claim.summary: CF4 plasma treatment produces omniphobic PVDF membrane resistant to wetting from oils and surfactants

evidence.verbatim_snippet: an omniphobic PVDF membrane was produced by CF4 plasma treatment. The membrane exhibited wetting resistance to different types of low surface tension liquids such as methanol, mineral oil and ethylene glycol

claim.summary: CF4 plasma PVDF membrane achieves 15.28 L/m²/h flux with near 100% salt rejection and stable performance

evidence.verbatim_snippet: The authors observed a high water vapour flux of 15.28 L m−2 h−1 and a near 100% salt rejection rate while exhibiting stable membrane performance

claim.summary: PFAS identified as emerging pollutants requiring treatment from groundwater contamination

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Another study was conducted using plasmas for the treatment of ground water. Atmospheric pressure Ar plasma was used to treat emerging pollutants such as perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS)

claim.summary: Perfluorohexanoic acid removed 90% by DBD plasma in 40 minutes

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Perfluorohexanoic acid DBD 90% removed 40 min

claim.summary: Perfluorohexane sulfonate 100% removed by DBD plasma in 40 minutes

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Perfluorahexane sulfonate DBD 100% removed 40 min

claim.summary: Perfluorheptane sulfonate 100% removed by DBD plasma in 40 minutes

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Perfluorheptane sulfonate DBD 100% removed 40 min

claim.summary: Perfluorooctanoic acid 100% removed by DBD plasma in 40 minutes

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Perfluorooctanoic acid DBD 100% removed 40 min

metadata.title: Per- and Polyfluorinated Alkyl Substances (PFAS) cycling within Michigan: Contaminated sites, landfills and wastewater treatment plants

claim.summary: PFAS are surfactants with excellent water-, grease-, and stain-resistant properties and high resistance to thermal degradation.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: PFAS are surfactants with excellent water-, grease-, and stain-resistant properties and high resistance to thermal degradation

claim.summary: PFAS have been mass produced since the 1940s and are used in industrial, commercial, military, and firefighting applications.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: PFAS have been mass produced since the 1940s (Dean et al., 2020) and are used in industrial, commercial, military, and firefighting applications

claim.summary: PFOA and PFOS are highly resistant to further degradation, earning PFAS the moniker 'forever chemicals'.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: The stability of PFAAs, most notably perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) has earned PFAS the moniker 'forever chemicals'

claim.summary: Some PFAS cause adverse health impacts at ng/L levels and bioaccumulate in humans and animals.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Some PFAS cause adverse health impacts at ng/L levels, accumulate in humans and animals, primarily through ingestion and bioaccumulate

claim.summary: Production and use of long-chain PFAS in North America, Europe, and Australia was voluntarily halted in the early 2000s.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: production and use of long-chain (≥ 8 carbons) PFAS in North America, Europe, and Australia was voluntarily halted in the early 2000s

claim.summary: Perfluorobutanesulfonic acid (PFBS) was adopted as a replacement for PFOS but may also have adverse health effects.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: perfluorobutanesulfonic acid (PFBS) (C4) was a replacement for PFOS (C8). Recent studies indicate that short-chain PFAS replacements are also persistent and can have adverse health and environmental effects

claim.summary: Short-chain PFAS have lower sorption and bioaccumulation tendencies but are more mobile in the environment than C8 compounds.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Short-chained PFAS have a lower tendency to sorb and bioaccumulate and are more mobile in the environment than C8 compounds

claim.summary: Technologies to remove PFAS from drinking water and groundwater collect and concentrate rather than destroy PFAS, creating treatment residual disposal challenges.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Technologies to remove PFAS from drinking water, leachate, and groundwater collect and concentrate rather than destroy PFAS. The treatment residuals must be disposed of in landfills

claim.summary: PFAS are detected in the remotest areas on earth, indicating widespread atmospheric transport.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: They are now detected in the remotest areas on earth (Butt et al., 2011; Miner et al., 2021)

claim.summary: Four dominant PFAS sources account for 75% of contaminated sites in Michigan: landfills, AFFF, metal platers, and automotive/metal stamping.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Four dominant PFAS sources – landfills, aqueous film-forming foams (AFFF), metal platers, and automotive/metal stamping – account for 75% of the contamination

claim.summary: Leachates from 19 landfills show diverse PFAS signatures with dominant compounds ranging from PFOA/PFOS to shorter-chain PFHxA, PFBA, and PFBS.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Diverse chemical signatures were observed for leachates collected from 19 landfills with the dominant PFAS ranging from perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) to shorter-chained compounds, perfluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA), perfluorobutanoic acid (PFBA), and perfluorobutanesulfonic acid (PFBS)

claim.summary: Analysis of landfill carbon chain length shows transition from C8s in older landfills to C4s and C6s in younger landfills, consistent with industry phase-out.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Analysis of PFAS carbon chain length as a function of landfill age shows the transition of C8s in leachate from older landfills to C4s and C6s in younger landfills, consistent with the phasing out and replacement of C8s

claim.summary: PFAS mass flux in landfill leachate ranges between 5-2,000 g/yr with highest values for active landfills.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: PFAS mass flux in leachate for landfills studied range between 5 – 2,000 g/yr and are highest for active landfills

claim.summary: WWTP effluent PFAS concentrations are as much as 19 times greater than influent, with some compounds increasing 20% to nearly 2,000%.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: effluent PFAS concentrations as much as 19 times greater than influent, attributed to transformations of unmeasured precursors in the influent to measured, stable PFAS in the effluent

claim.summary: PFOS concentrations decreased across 6 WWTPs, consistent with sorption onto biosolids.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: PFOS concentrations decreased across 6 WWTPs, consistent with a strong tendency to adsorb onto biosolids

claim.summary: Estimated mass of discharge of mostly unregulated PFAS from WWTPs to receiving waters ranges from 40 g/yr to 128 kg/yr.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Estimated mass of discharge of (mostly unregulated) PFAS from WWTPs to receiving waters range from 40 g/yr to 128 kg/yr

claim.summary: Polyfluoroalkyl substances and fluorotelomers break down in the environment to form perfluoroalkyl acids (PFAAs) which are highly resistant to further degradation.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Polyfluoroalkyl substances, fluorotelomers, and other polymers breakdown in the environment to form perfluoroalkyl acids (PFAAs), which are highly resistant to further degradation

claim.summary: PFAS are released to the environment via waste disposal, landfill leachate, WWTP residuals, AFFF use, and direct industrial release.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: They are released to the environment via waste disposal, landfill leachate, residuals from wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs), use of aqueous film-forming foams (AFFF), and direct release from industry

claim.summary: Michigan required biosolids with PFOA + PFOS between 20-150 µg/kg for land application; those above 150 µg/kg must be landfilled or treated.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Biosolids with PFOA + PFOS between 20 µg/kg and 150 µg/kg may be land applied, but biosolids with PFOA + PFOS greater than 150 µg/kg must be landfilled or treated

claim.summary: Michigan has developed one of the most complete PFAS datasets due to proactive regulatory standards.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Due to proactive regulatory standards, Michigan has developed one of the most complete PFAS datasets available for this purpose

claim.summary: Michigan required 28 PFAS compounds to be tested, exceeding USEPA Method 537.1 which only covers 18 compounds.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: At the time of this study, Michigan required 28 compounds to be tested (Table 1) which is not possible with USEPA Method 537.1

claim.summary: In 2016, USEPA issued a drinking water health advisory limit for PFOA + PFOS at 70 ng/L.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: In 2016, USEPA issued a drinking water health advisory limit for PFOA + PFOS at 70 ng/L

extractions.compound: PFBS, PFHxS, PFHxA, PFOS, PFOA, PFNA, GenX

claim.summary: Michigan promulgated MCLs for 7 PFAS compounds in August 2020: PFBS 420 ng/L, PFHxS 51 ng/L, PFHxA 400,000 ng/L, PFOS 16 ng/L, PFOA 8 ng/L, PFNA 6 ng/L, GenX 370 ng/L.

evidence.verbatim_snippet: new MCLs for drinking water were promulgated for seven compounds: PFBS 420 ng/L, perfluorohexanesulfonic acid (PFHxS) 51 ng/L, PFHxA 400,000 ng/L, PFOS 16 ng/L, PFOA 8 ng/L, perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA) 6 ng/L, hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (HFPO-DA/Gen X) 370 ng/L

metadata.title: Perfluorochemicals in water reuse

claim.summary: Perfluorochemicals are used in food packaging, paints, and lubricants

evidence.verbatim_snippet: They are used in a variety of materials such as food packaging, paints, and lubricants

claim.summary: PFOA and PFOS have been detected in wastewater globally

evidence.verbatim_snippet: detected in wastewater (Alzaga and Bayona, 2004; Boulanger et al., 2005)

claim.summary: PFOA and PFOS detected in surface water, groundwater, and drinking water

evidence.verbatim_snippet: detected in surface water, groundwater, drinking water, and rain

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Laboratory studies demonstrate that mammals readily absorb PFOA and PFOS during oral and inhalation exposures. They tend to distribute to the blood serum and the liver and can cross the blood-brain and placental barriers

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Perfluorochemicals bioaccumulate and have been detected in biota around the world, including fish, seals, minks, albatross, bald eagles, polar bears, and humans

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Typical concentrations of PFOA and PFOS in the serum of non-occupationally exposed humans are 3–35 and 7–82 µg/l, respectively

claim.summary: Adverse effects observed in rats at 370 µg/l PFOA, differing from human levels by less than a safety factor of 100

evidence.verbatim_snippet: adverse effects have been observed in rats at levels (370 µg/l PFOA) which differ from humans by less than a safety factor of 100

claim.summary: PFOS concentrations in ringed seals reach 8-242 µg/l serum

evidence.verbatim_snippet: Wildlife monitoring studies for high trophic levels report PFOS concentrations of 8–242 µg/l serum in ringed seals

claim.summary: PFOS concentrations in albatross blood are 3-34 µg/l

evidence.verbatim_snippet: 3–34 µg/l blood in albatross

claim.summary: PFOS concentrations in red panda serum are 0.8-74 µg/l

evidence.verbatim_snippet: 0.8–74 µg/l serum in red panda

claim.summary: Perfluorochemicals persist through wastewater treatment

evidence.verbatim_snippet: persistence of perfluorochemicals in wastewater treatment

claim.summary: 90-470 ng/l perfluorochemicals detected in recycled water from four California wastewater treatment plants

evidence.verbatim_snippet: In the recycled water, 90–470 ng/l perfluorochemicals were detected

claim.summary: PFOA concentrations of 10-190 ng/l in recycled water

evidence.verbatim_snippet: predominantly perfluorooctanoate (PFOA; 10–190 ng/l)

claim.summary: PFOS concentrations of 20-190 ng/l in recycled water

evidence.verbatim_snippet: perfluorooctanesulfonate (PFOS; 20–190 ng/l)

claim.summary: No significant removal of perfluorochemicals was observed in a constructed wetland treatment system

evidence.verbatim_snippet: No significant removal of perfluorochemicals was observed in the wetland (total concentration ranged 100–170 ng/l across various treatment stages)

claim.summary: N-EtFOSAA, PFDS, and PFOS were dominant perfluorochemicals in wetland treatment stages

evidence.verbatim_snippet: 2-(N-ethylperfluorooctanesulfonamido) acetic acid (N-EtFOSAA), perfluorodecanesulfonate (PFDS), and PFOS were dominant

claim.summary: Perfluorochemicals detected in surface water and groundwater at Upper Silver and Coyote Creeks at 20-150 ng/l total

evidence.verbatim_snippet: perfluorochemicals were found in the surface water and underlying groundwater at a total of 20–150 ng/l with PFOS and PFOA again making the largest contribution

claim.summary: Perfluorochemical release via recycled water into sensitive ecosystems requires ecotoxicological evaluation

evidence.verbatim_snippet: With respect to ecotoxicological effects, perfluorochemical release via recycled water into sensitive ecosystems requires evaluation

claim.summary: PFOA in WWTP 2 reclaimed wastewater: 180 ng/l

evidence.verbatim_snippet: WWTP 2: PFOA 180 ng/l

claim.summary: PFOS in WWTP 2 reclaimed wastewater: 190 ng/l

evidence.verbatim_snippet: WWTP 2: PFOS 190 ng/l

claim.summary: N-EtFOSAA is a precursor to PFOS; biodegrades to PFOS slowly; higher concentrations of N-EtFOSAA than PFOS expected in wastewater effluent

evidence.verbatim_snippet: higher concentrations of N-EtFOSAA rather than PFOS in wastewater effluent are expected given the biodegradation kinetics of 2-(N-ethylperfluorooctanesulfonamido) ethanol (N-EtFOSE), a precursor to N-EtFOSAA that is used in protective paper coatings. N-EtFOSAA then biodegrades to PFOS, but more slowly.

claim.summary: Perfluorochemicals resist biodegradation and sorption is limited

evidence.verbatim_snippet: perfluorochemicals monitored resist biodegradation and sorption is limited

claim.summary: Tier II screening value of 1200 ng/l PFOS (aquatic chronic value) established by EPA methodology

evidence.verbatim_snippet: A more conservative Tier II (potential risk) screening value of 1200 ng/l PFOS (aquatic chronic value) was determined by Beach et al. (2005) using EPA methodology

metadata.title: PFAS removal by ion exchange resins: A review

claim.summary: PFAS are extensively used in common consumer products such as non-stick cookware, specialized garments, fire-fighting foams and stain resistant coatings

evidence.verbatim_snippet: PFAS are extensively used in common consumer products such as non-stick cookware, specialized garments, fire-fighting foams and stain resistant coatings

evidence.verbatim_snippet: These anthropogenic compounds typically consist of a long hydrophobic perfluorinated carbon chain (CnF2nþ1) and a hydrophilic functional group such as eSO3-

claim.summary: Several PFAS have been linked to cancer, liver/kidney damage and developmental effects in mammals

evidence.verbatim_snippet: In recent years, several PFAS have been linked to cancer, liver/kidney damage and developmental effects in mammals

claim.summary: General population is potentially exposed to PFAS through consumption of contaminated drinking water

evidence.verbatim_snippet: The general population is potentially exposed to PFAS through consumption of contaminated drinking water

claim.summary: Emerging PFAS contaminants have been detected in waters across the globe including GenX, Fe53B, ADONA and other ether PFAS

Ammonium fluoride is used only as a minor electrolyte component during electrode synthesis and does not contain persistent fluorinated compounds (PFAS). The paper does not discuss fluoropolymers, PFOA, PFOS, GenX, or other persistent fluorinated organic compounds. While fluoride ions are used, they are not bioaccumulative fluorinated compounds and the paper contains no discussion of fluorinated compound lifecycle, environmental persistence, health effects, regulatory action, or the particular concerns associated with PFAS/fluoropolymers.

claim.summary: APS-initiated PVDF with sulfate end groups showed 5% weight loss at only 315°C, indicating lower thermal stability.

claim.summary: APFO surfactant was found to be unnecessary for PVDF polymerization and removal improved CF3 chain-end content from 40% to 85%.

claim.summary: CF3-PVDF with lower molar mass (30,000 g/mol) achieved similar 1% weight loss temperature to commercial Kynar (400,000 g/mol Mn).
